q-95746.name: Question 1
q-95746.problem:
Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, approximate the probability that a student gets $14$ correct answers on a true/false quiz with $25$ questions if the student answers all questions at random. Give your final answer to three decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.4\,$ | $\,0.6554\,$ | $\,0.6591\,$ | $\,0.6628\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7257\,$ | $\,0.7291\,$ | $\,0.7324\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.7881\,$ | $\,0.7910\,$ | $\,0.7939\,$ |
q-95746.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=25$ and $p=0.5.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =25\cdot 0.5 \\  & =12.5 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =25\cdot (1-0.5) \\  & =12.5 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(25)(0.5)=12.5
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(25)(0.5)(1-0.5)=6.25.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(12.5,6.25).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=14).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=14)≈P(13.5\le Y\le 14.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(13.5\le Y\le 14.5) & =P(\frac{13.5-12.5}{\sqrt{6.25}}\le Z\le \frac{14.5-12.5}{\sqrt{6.25}}) \\  & ≈P(0.40\le Z\le 0.80) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.80)-P(Z<0.40) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.80)-P(Z\le 0.40) \\  & =Φ(0.80)-Φ(0.40) \\  & =0.7881-0.6554 \\  & =0.1327\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=14)≈0.133.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.1327.$

q-95758.name: Question 2
q-95758.problem:
It is known that $43%$ of the users of a newspaper's website purchase a digital subscription. Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, estimate the probability that in a random sample of $200$ users, more than $80$ but less than $105$ of them purchase a digital subscription. Give your final answer to three decimal places. *Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$$\,0.09\,$
$\,-0.8\,$ $\,0.1922\,$ $\,0.1894\,$ $\,0.1867\,$
$\,-0.7\,$ $\,0.2206\,$ $\,0.2177\,$ $\,0.2148\,$
$\,-0.6\,$ $\,0.2514\,$ $\,0.2483\,$ $\,0.2451\,$
$z$$\,0.02\,$$\,0.03\,$$\,0.04\,$
$\,2.5\,$ $\,0.9941\,$ $\,0.9943\,$ $\,0.9945\,$
$\,2.6\,$ $\,0.9956\,$ $\,0.9957\,$ $\,0.9959\,$
$\,2.7\,$ $\,0.9967\,$ $\,0.9968\,$ $\,0.9969\,$
q-95758.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=200$ and $p=0.43.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =200\cdot 0.43 \\  & =86 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =200\cdot (1-0.43) \\  & =114 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(200)(0.43)=86
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(200)(0.43)(1-0.43)=49.02.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(86,49.02).$

Now, we can estimate the desired probability $P(80<X<105).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(80<X<105)=P(81\le X\le 104)≈P(80.5\le Y\le 104.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(80.5\le Y<104.5) & =P(\frac{80.5-86}{\sqrt{49.02}}\le Z\le \frac{104.5-86}{\sqrt{49.02}}) \\  & ≈P(-0.79\le Z\le 2.64) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.64)-P(Z<-0.79) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.64)-P(Z\le -0.79) \\  & =Φ(2.64)-Φ(-0.79) \\  & =0.9959-0.2148 \\  & =0.7811\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(80<X<105)≈0.781.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of
$0.7798.$

q-132286.problem:
Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, approximate the probability that $58$ people say "yes" on a yes/no survey in a randomly selected sample of $100$ people if the probability that a person answers "yes" is $0.5.$ Give your final answer to three decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.5\,$ | $\,0.9332\,$ | $\,0.9345\,$ | $\,0.9357\,$ |
| $\,1.6\,$ | $\,0.9452\,$ | $\,0.9463\,$ | $\,0.9474\,$ |
| $\,1.7\,$ | $\,0.9554\,$ | $\,0.9564\,$ | $\,0.9573\,$ |
q-132286.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=100$ and $p=0.5.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =100\cdot 0.5 \\  & =50 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =100\cdot (1-0.5) \\  & =50 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(100)(0.5)=50
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(100)(0.5)(1-0.5)=25.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(50,25).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=58).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=58)≈P(57.5\le Y\le 58.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(57.5\le Y\le 58.5) & =P(\frac{57.5-50}{\sqrt{25}}\le Z\le \frac{58.5-50}{\sqrt{25}}) \\  & ≈P(1.5\le Z\le 1.7) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.7)-P(Z<1.5) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.7)-P(Z\le 1.5) \\  & =Φ(1.7)-Φ(1.5) \\  & =0.9554-0.9332 \\  & =0.022\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=58)≈0.022.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0223.$

q-132504.name: Question 5
q-132504.problem:
Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, approximate the probability that a fair spinner with five regions: red, green, orange, white, and blue, lands on green or white more than $25$ but less than $35$ times out of $80$ spins. Give your final answer to three decimal places. *Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$$\,0.09\,$
$\,-1.5\,$ $\,0.0582\,$ $\,0.0570\,$ $\,0.0559\,$
$\,-1.4\,$ $\,0.0708\,$ $\,0.0694\,$ $\,0.0681\,$
$\,-1.3\,$ $\,0.0854\,$ $\,0.0838\,$ $\,0.0823\,$
$z$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$$\,0.09\,$
$\,0.4\,$ $\,0.6808\,$ $\,0.6844\,$ $\,0.6879\,$
$\,0.5\,$ $\,0.7157\,$ $\,0.7190\,$ $\,0.7224\,$
$\,0.6\,$ $\,0.7486\,$ $\,0.7518\,$ $\,0.7549\,$
q-132504.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=80$ and $p=0.4.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =80\cdot 0.4 \\  & =32 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =80\cdot (1-0.4) \\  & =48 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(80)(0.4)=32
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(80)(0.4)(1-0.4)=19.2.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(32,19.2).$

Now, we can estimate the desired probability $P(25<X<35).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(25<X<35)=P(26\le X\le 34)≈P(25.5\le Y\le 34.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(25.5\le Y\le 34.5) & =P(\frac{25.5-32}{\sqrt{19.2}}\le Z\le \frac{34.5-32}{\sqrt{19.2}}) \\  & ≈P(-1.48\le Z\le 0.57) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.57)-P(Z<-1.48) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.57)-P(Z\le -1.48) \\  & =Φ(0.57)-Φ(-1.48) \\  & =0.7157-0.0694 \\  & =0.6463\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(25<X<35)≈0.646.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of
$0.65.$
